newsitem.title: USA: Calif. revenue drop 'bears watching' - finance dept.
newsitem.headline: Calif. revenue drop 'bears watching' - finance dept.

text.p: California's Department of Finance on Thursday said June's shortfall in personal income tax revenues "bears watching," but could just be a statistical blip.

"It's something that certainly bears watching," department spokesman H.D. Palmer said. But he added; "One month's numbers do not a trend make. You've got to take a look at how these numbers come in over several months."
California general fund revenues for June fell $74 million below the budget forecast of $5.6 billion, the department said in a report on Wednesday.

Personal income tax revenues were $94 million below the month's forecast of $2.38 billion. For the year, personal income tax revenues were $222 million below the budget forecast, the Department of Finance said.
Palmer said June revenues reflected the governor's May budget revision, which forecast a sharp $2.3 billion increase in revenues for fiscal years 1996-1997 and 1997-1998.
Other state revenue categories in June came in just above or just below the governor's forecast, suggesting the May budget revision was on target, state officials said.
Sales and use tax revenues were $8 million above the month's estimate of $1.7 billion. For the year, these revenues were up $94 million, or 0.6 percent, the department said.
Bank and corporation tax revenues were $1 million below the month's estimate of $1.1 billion. For the year, they were $22 million above forecast, the department said.
Revenues from the insurance, alcoholic beverage, horse racing, estate and tobacco taxes were $3 million below the state's budget forecast of $324 million.
The remaining revenues -- pooled money interest, trial court funding, and other categories -- were $16 million above the month's forecast of $105 million.
